title: Computational analysis of MYC gene variants: structural and functional impact of non-synonymous SNPs.
authors: Bhuyan, Plabita; Bharali, Varshabi; Basumatary, Sangju; Lego, Aido; Sarma, Juman; Borbora, Debasish
one_liner_zh: 该文用29种计算工具分析MYC基因nsSNP对蛋白结构、稳定性及MYC/MAX蛋白-蛋白互作的影响，虽涉及转录因子MYC但聚焦SNP致病性评估，未深入TF-DNA结合建模，方法以序列预测和对接为主，与TF-DNA互作课题部分相关。
abstract: The MYC proto-oncogene encodes a basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (HLH-LZ) transcription factor, acting as a master regulator of genes involved in cellular proliferation, differentiation, and immune surveillance. Dysregulation of MYC is implicated in over 70% of human cancers, driving oncogenic processes through altered gene expression and disrupted cellular functions. Non-synonymous single nucleotide polymorphisms (nsSNPs) within coding regions can significantly impact protein structure and function, leading to abnormal cellular behaviours. This study employed 29 in silico tools to systematically evaluate the deleteriousness of nsSNPs within the MYC gene. These tools assessed the variants' effects on protein structure, disease association, functional domains, and post-translational modification sites. This study investigated if these variants may disrupt protein-protein interactions, critical for MYC's oncogenic roles and normal cellular functions. Our analysis identified 21 nsSNPs that were predicted to be deleterious and pathogenic. These variants correspond to residues D63H, D63Y, P74L, P75L, N375D, N375I, E378K, E378Q, E378A, E378G, E378V, R379P, R381K, R381T, R382W, L392P, R393C, R393H, R393P, L411H, and L411P. Stability assessments indicated that these variants could destabilise the MYC protein. None of the variants affected post-translational modifications. Protein-protein interaction and docking analysis revealed that variants within bHLH and LZ domains may disrupt MYC/MAX binding, potentially impacting MYC's oncogenic activity and transcriptional regulation. This computational assessment enhances our understanding of genetic variations within the MYC gene and prioritises candidate nsSNPs for experimental validation and therapeutic exploration.
abstract_zh: MYC原癌基因编码一种碱性螺旋-环-螺旋亮氨酸拉链（HLH-LZ）转录因子，作为参与细胞增殖、分化和免疫监视的基因的主调控因子。MYC的失调与超过70%的人类癌症相关，通过改变基因表达和破坏细胞功能驱动致癌过程。编码区内的非同义单核苷酸多态性（nsSNPs）可显著影响蛋白质结构和功能，导致异常细胞行为。本研究采用29种计算机模拟工具系统评估MYC基因内nsSNPs的有害性。这些工具评估了变异对蛋白质结构、疾病关联、功能结构域和翻译后修饰位点的影响。本研究调查了这些变异是否可能破坏蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用，该相互作用对MYC的致癌作用和正常细胞功能至关重要。我们的分析识别出21个被预测为有害且致病的nsSNPs。这些变异对应残基D63H、D63Y、P74L、P75L、N375D、N375I、E378K、E378Q、E378A、E378G、E378V、R379P、R381K、R381T、R382W、L392P、R393C、R393H、R393P、L411H和L411P。稳定性评估表明这些变异可能使MYC蛋白不稳定。所有变异均未影响翻译后修饰。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用和对接分析显示，bHLH和LZ结构域内的变异可能破坏MYC/MAX结合，潜在影响MYC的致癌活性和转录调控。这项计算评估增进了我们对MYC基因内遗传变异的理解，并优先筛选出候选nsSNPs以供实验验证和治疗探索。
